html:
The Naskapi are an Innu people of the interior of the Quebec-Labrador peninsula. St'aschinuw means "our land". Their language is close to Innu and Cree.

They lived by hunting caribou, following the great herds across the tundra and open forest, and fished in the lakes. Their kin to the south were the Montagnais, and to the north lived the Inuit of Nunavik.

The Hudson's Bay Company traded with them from posts such as Fort Chimo. When the caribou failed in the early 1900s, many starved. In 1956 the government moved them to Schefferville, a new iron mining town. Under the Northeastern Quebec Agreement of 1978 they gained their own village, Kawawachikamach. See also Naskapi Innu and Nitassinan.
